text:
maria: Heads-up — escalated ticket from Acme Finance: streaming responses intermittently hang and never deliver the final [DONE] when the user's oauth token rotates mid-stream. Happening ~2-3x/day for them, reproducible in our env if you rotate token while a long-lived SSE is active.

kevin: roughly which SDK/version + deployment mode? any logs?

maria: Go SDK v0.9.2 (dedicated), customer on Redwood Private behind their LB. Token TTL set to 60s, client refresh at 50s. Repro steps below. Logs show connection stays open, no new data, client iterator blocks. Server shows continued write activity.

maria: repro steps I used:
```bash
# start a stream with a short-lived token
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_TOKEN\" \ 
  -N \"https://private-redwood.example.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-test\"
# wait 30s and rotate token in the client (simulate refresh)
# client issues new connection with fresh token while old one still active
```

anya: I reproduced quickly on py SDK (1.3.0) — iterator yields some data, then stalls. On server we still emit events (heartbeat and partial choices). The Python client never receives the terminating event. stack trace shows coroutine blocked in `read_event()` awaiting newline.

kevin: do we have any headers we add for resume semantics? e.g., sequence IDs or resume tokens?

maria: yes — when stream reconnects we send `X-Resume-Seq` and `X-Client-Stream-Id`. Customer flow is: client opens new connection with same Stream-Id after refresh. Server emits `event: resume\ndata: {"seq":123}` then continues.

liam: interesting — I saw a similar symptom in a repro: if the old connection is closed due to token invalidation but the TCP FIN+RST race happens, the server's SSE chunk boundary can be split such that the last line doesn't end in `\n\n` and our Go parser uses `bufio.Scanner` which silently drops the final unterminated token. That would leave the client waiting for the final blank line that denotes end-of-event.

anya: here's the minimal trace I captured (py):
```
... event: choices
data: {"text":"... partial"}
# then we got a half-chunk: "data: {\"text\":\"final fragment"
# connection reset occurrs here
```
Client never gets `\n\n` so coroutine waits.

kevin: that fits. Does Go SDK treat buffered partial lines differently from Py?

liam: yes — the Go SSE parser uses `bufio.NewScanner(conn)` with default token split on `\n`. If the last token is not newline-terminated, Scanner will return it on `Scan()` but only once; however if the reader returns io.ErrUnexpectedEOF it's possible a call pattern results in dropping the final fragment depending on how we interleave cancellation. There's also a bug where after we call `Cancel()` in the reconnect code path we don't drain the `data` channel before reusing the stream id, leading to the iterator API never seeing the trailing blank line.

maria: can reproduce reliably by: open stream -> wait 35s -> trigger token refresh + immediate reconnect -> old socket gets RST -> server emits resume + final event, client blocks.

kevin: any chance this also caused double-billing / duplicate tokens? customer complained about duplicate partials previously.

liam: potential for duplicate partials if both connections are accepted by server for a brief window. But in this repro the issue is hanging rather than duplication. Still worth checking billing logs for overlapping active sessions with same Stream-Id.

anya: created a small py repro gist: https://gist.github.com/anya/stream-hang-repro — it reproduces with our py SDK by forcing refresh inside the event loop.

maria: I grabbed server-side logs for Acme: shows write succeeded after resume, then client-side stops acknowledging.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: patch/go-sdk-sse-fix (#4389) — CI pending.

liam: patch summary: ensure parser treats unterminated final chunks as complete events when connection closes or when the connection is cancelled, and in reconnect path we drain the old stream's event queue before returning EOF to the iterator. Also add a small grace window on server to emit final blank line when sequencing a resume event.

kevin: can you link the PR and a short test we can run? customer is asking for ETA.

liam: PR here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4389 — includes unit test that simulates RST after partial line; also integration test that toggles token mid-stream. If CI goes green we can roll to staging today.

maria: thanks — I've told Acme support we have a fix and requested permission to run a staging build in their sandbox. Will confirm once deployed to staging.

support-bot: SUMMARY: root cause = client reconnect race + parser handling of unterminated SSE chunks. Impact = some SDKs (Go, Py) hang on iterator end when token rotates mid-stream. Mitigation = restart client on token rotate (workaround), patch merged for Go and additional tests for Py. Next steps: roll fix to staging, monitor customer sandbox, and scan billing logs for overlapping sessions.

kevin: noted. please update this thread with staging results and any customer repro logs. :thumbsup:

maria: will do. patch deployed to staging 1901234625, Acme confirmed staging replayed their broken session and finished successfully. Closing the loop with them now.

support-bot: Ticket ACME-789 updated: status -> awaiting customer confirmation (staging validated).
